discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) predicted that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees, the Dirac bands of bilayer graphene become nearly flat, so that interactions dominate kinetic energy. Jarillo-Herrero (2018) achieved this experimentally with tear-and-stack fabrication, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity tunable by a gate in a single device. Together, theory and experiment created 'twistronics': the twist angle became a new, continuously tunable knob for the electronic structure of quantum matter. This opened a field that hundreds of groups worldwide now pursue. Moiré systems in graphene and transition-metal dichalcogenides have since revealed Mott insulators, generalized Wigner crystals, orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect and fractional Chern insulators at zero magnetic field. Rarely has a simple conceptual idea, realized with such experimental elegance, so profoundly changed what physicists can engineer and measure in strongly correlated, topological matter.
